33 QUESTIONS EXECUTIVES ASK ABOUT AI—ANSWERED https://every.


EVERY'S CONSULTING TEAM ANSWERS 400 EXECUTIVES ON STRATEGY, SKEPTICS, GOVERNANCE, AND RESTRUCTURING FOR AI https://every.

by Natalia Quintero https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiMzMgUXVlc3Rpb25zIEV4ZWN1dGl2ZXMgQXNrIEFib3V0IEFJ4oCUQW5zd2VyZWQgIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDI5OSwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZXZlcnkudG8vQG5hdGFsaWFfMjk0NCIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjozfQ== and Mike Taylor https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiMzMgUXVlc3Rpb25zIEV4ZWN1dGl2ZXMgQXNrIEFib3V0IEFJ4oCUQW5zd2VyZWQgIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDI5OSwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZXZlcnkudG8vQG1pa2VfMjExNCIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo0fQ==

Midjourney/Every illustration.

Natalia Quintero https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiMzMgUXVlc3Rpb25zIEV4ZWN1dGl2ZXMgQXNrIEFib3V0IEFJ4oCUQW5zd2VyZWQgIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDI5OSwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZXZlcnkudG8vQG5hdGFsaWFfMjk0NCIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo1fQ==, who leads Every’s consulting practice, has spoken with more than 100 companies about AI adoption, including the New York Times and the hedge fund Walleye Capital https://every.. In June, she and Mike Taylor https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiMzMgUXVlc3Rpb25zIEV4ZWN1dGl2ZXMgQXNrIEFib3V0IEFJ4oCUQW5zd2VyZWQgIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDI5OSwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZXZlcnkudG8vQG1pa2VfMjExNCIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo3fQ==—now Every’s head of evals practice—hosted a live webinar for 400 executives on how organizations can adopt and implement AI without stalling out. More questions came in than they could answer live, so afterward they wrote up 33 of them—covering strategy, winning over skeptics, tool selection, governance, and how to restructure a company for an AI-native future. That document went only to attendees at the time; we’re making it public for the first time here.—Kate Lee https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiMzMgUXVlc3Rpb25zIEV4ZWN1dGl2ZXMgQXNrIEFib3V0IEFJ4oCUQW5zd2VyZWQgIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDI5OSwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZXZlcnkudG8vQGthdGVfMTc2NyIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo4fQ==

----------------------------------------



When you put a room full of executives in front of two AI consultants and let them ask anything, you learn about where organizations are stuck with this technology. Here are all the questions that came up on our live session on June 2—from how to get skeptics on board to keeping context fresh.

Every Consulting https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiMzMgUXVlc3Rpb25zIEV4ZWN1dGl2ZXMgQXNrIEFib3V0IEFJ4oCUQW5zd2VyZWQgIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDI5OSwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZXZlcnkudG8vY29uc3VsdGluZyIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo5fQ== works with tech and finance teams to implement AI across their workflows, from strategy to training to building the actual tools.


STRATEGY AND ORGANIZATIONAL TRANSFORMATION

Q: How do you get teams to think bigger about change? Not just getting the work done faster, but rethinking how the work is done?

A: Give your most AI-curious staff permission to build ambitious projects. It’s easier to raise the ceiling than the floor. It’s easier for one AI-fluent person to create 10 good skills and do 10 times the work than it is to get 10 people to each create one skill or double their output. Once that’s in place, set a vision, designate AI champions, prove out high-value skills, then scale.

Q: What does a good vision for AI adoption look like?

A: AI is a tool, not a strategy. A good vision applies AI to your company’s strategic roadmap and allows you to tackle parts of it that were impossible before.

For example: customer service. There’s effectively infinite demand for it, and it’s too expensive to staff the phones enough to get wait times down to a few minutes. Even then, the person that your customer talks to might not have the context the best customer representative has. AI is a great leveler here. It makes it cheaper to serve every customer quickly, it gives every representative full context by allowing them to search for it live, and it can pre-emptively answer questions before anyone gets on the phone. That’s what a good vision looks like: ambitious and finally affordable because of AI.

Q: Do you need to convince skeptics? How do you get them over the hump of seeing value in adopting AI?

A: Rather than focusing efforts on convincing skeptics, highlight AI champions. When AI champions, often skeptics’ own peers, demonstrate how they are getting value from AI tools, others start doing it out of practicality. Pair that with demos of new AI tools or skills that are relevant to your teams.

I’d also encourage side projects. People with side projects are much further ahead on AI because they can take bigger risks than they can at work, by using tools that aren’t on the approved vendor list, and by pushing the limits of what works. Previously, a manager might feel uncomfortable about that. Now, I’d be disappointed if an employee didn’t have a side project, because it means they don’t have the space to experiment, play, and take bigger risks.

Q: Is there a tension between using AI for productivity and using it to pursue bigger ambitions—and how do you think about the balance?

There are two kinds of productivity: doing what you already do faster, and doing things you otherwise wouldn’t be doing. That second one is vision. You can’t only focus on productivity, but once you solve the productivity problem and automate what you already do, you’ll start looking for new things to do. Prioritize existing pain points for immediate value and place strategic bets on bigger products.

OUR CHATGPT AND OPENCLAW GUIDES JUST GOT AN OVERHAUL https://every.


NEW APPS, TOOLS, AND SETUP—HERE’S WHAT WE CHANGED AND WHY https://every.

by Katie Parrott https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiT3VyIENoYXRHUFQgYW5kIE9wZW5DbGF3IEd1aWRlcyBKdXN0IEdvdCBhbiBPdmVyaGF1bCIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0NTMsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL0BrYXRpZS5wYXJyb3R0MTIiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6M30=

Midjourney/Every illustration.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiT3VyIENoYXRHUFQgYW5kIE9wZW5DbGF3IEd1aWRlcyBKdXN0IEdvdCBhbiBPdmVyaGF1bCIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0NTMsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL2NvbnRleHQtd2luZG93IiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjR9 to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



We talk about AI progress like it’s a race between models. That’s the part with version numbers, and what you argue about over dinner. But the model is only one piece. It reaches your work through the app you open it in, the files and tools you let it touch, the instructions you’ve saved from last time, and the person keeping all of that from going stale. Any of those can change your results as much as a new model would—sometimes more.

We rewrote two of our guides this week. The models didn’t change. The infrastructure around them that governs their behavior and capabilities did. These guides are written as much for agents as for humans, so share them with your agent and ask it: “What can we learn from this that we can adapt for how we work?”


KNOWLEDGE WORK HAS A HOME IN CHATGPT NOW

When we initially wrote our Codex for Knowledge Work guide, the idea of using a coding-agent interface for something other than coding was so new that even OpenAI hadn’t built a dedicated home for it. Now it has. Quick questions stay in Chat, longer assignments move to Work, and software jobs go to Codex. For knowledge workers who don’t touch code, the vast majority of your tasks can be handled by Work.

We’ve retitled the guide ChatGPT for Knowledge Work https://every. and rewritten it around that new setup. The guide keeps its 16 workflows, but recasts most of them for Work. The update also covers several features that didn’t exist when we wrote the original guide:

 * Goals: Type /goal to turn an objective into a persistent goal with a definition of done.
 * Projects: Choose between ChatGPT projects, which keep cloud conversations, files, and instructions together, and local projects, which give Work or Codex access to a folder on your computer.
 * Scheduled work: Use Scheduled Tasks for recurring jobs in Work and thread automations for longer loops in Codex.
 * Browser access: The app’s built-in browser has its own signed-in profile. Choose Chrome when a task needs your existing sessions, tabs, or extensions.

Read ChatGPT for Knowledge Work https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiT3VyIENoYXRHUFQgYW5kIE9wZW5DbGF3IEd1aWRlcyBKdXN0IEdvdCBhbiBPdmVyaGF1bCIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0NTMsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL2d1aWRlcy9jb2RleC1mb3Ita25vd2xlZGdlLXdvcms_c291cmNlPXBvc3RfYnV0dG9uIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjZ9

https://every.




MOST AI TOOLS STOP AT THE SUMMARY

Research is the easy part. The work is everything after: the report drafted, the spreadsheet updated, the recap posted in Slack, the follow-up actually sent. Grok Bot’s Bots do that part. Each one runs on its own cloud computer, signed in to your CRM, your ATS, your inbox, clicking and typing through the same software your team already uses. Give a Bot a job instead of a prompt, then check the result the way you’d check a coworker’s. Built by the team behind SpaceXAI.

Put a Bot to work https://every.
Want to sponsor Every? Click here https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiT3VyIENoYXRHUFQgYW5kIE9wZW5DbGF3IEd1aWRlcyBKdXN0IEdvdCBhbiBPdmVyaGF1bCIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0NTMsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJtYWlsdG86c3BvbnNvcnNoaXBzQGV2ZXJ5LnRvIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjl9.


OUR OPENCLAW RECOMMENDATION CHANGED

Our first OpenClaw guide https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiT3VyIENoYXRHUFQgYW5kIE9wZW5DbGF3IEd1aWRlcyBKdXN0IEdvdCBhbiBPdmVyaGF1bCIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0NTMsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL2d1aWRlcy9jbGF3LXNjaG9vbCIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjoxMH0= focused on the appeal of a personal agent. A Claw lives in your messaging app, connects to tools you authorize, and keeps doing recurring jobs without a fresh prompt. For someone willing to maintain it, that setup can still be unusually useful.

The update adds what we learned from running Claws ourselves. A stronger model still can’t log in when a credential expires. It can’t notice that an integration broke last week, or that a job you set up months ago should’ve been turned off. Putting the agent on a server keeps it running—but somebody still has to keep its tools connected, its permissions current, and its memory from filling up wtih stale instructions. For now, that somebody is a burden.

If you already track your workouts, steps, heart rate, or screen time, sleep is usually the next thing you start wondering about.

SomniPods 3 are sleep earbuds that also track movement overnight, so you can see more of what happened while you were asleep without wearing a watch or ring.

They’re also designed to solve the more immediate problem: actually getting through the night comfortably. Each bud weighs 3.3g, sits low in the ear, and combines Hybrid ANC, passive isolation, and sleep sounds to help reduce nighttime noise.

There’s even a private in-ear alarm, which is useful if you wake up earlier than the person next to you.

So yes, they’re earbuds. But they’re much closer to a piece of sleep gear than another pair of headphones.

#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/c3c5e9d8-c1aa-4850-b400-31256b4708f0/Hugging-Face-team__1_.png?t=1787839176)
Caption: Courtesy: Clement Delangue, co-founder of Hugging Face

**1/ Nvidia is buying Hugging Face for $12.9B** - The Information [reports](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/nvidia-agrees-buy-open-source-model-repository-hugging-face-12-9-billion) Nvidia has agreed to buy the open-source AI platform, which hosts millions of models and datasets and is basically where a huge chunk of the open AI ecosystem lives. This gives the AI chip giant control of one of the world’s most important platforms for open-source models and datasets. Nvidia previously offered $500M for a stake at a $7B valuation, but Hugging Face turned it down.

The interesting bit is what happens to the platform’s neutrality. Hugging Face supports models running on Nvidia, AMD, Google and others, while Nvidia now owns the whole thing.

Hugging Face was last valued at $4.5B in 2023. Nvidia is paying almost 3x that now.

Feels like Nvidia is slowly trying to own every layer of the AI stack.

**2/ The Ox Alpha mystery is finally solved** - Z AI revealed that the anonymous model that took over OpenRouter last week was actually its new [GLM-5.3-Flash](https://z.ai/blog/glm-5.3-flash). They’d been running it anonymously to get real-world feedback, and it ended up becoming the most [popular model](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) of the week.

The interesting bit: the whole thing was running on Chinese AI chips. Z AI says the setup got its serving costs down to roughly Nvidia-level economics, which is probably more interesting than the mystery itself.

They also released the weights under MIT and say it scores 57 on Artificial Analysis at $0.045 per task on the discounted price, roughly 10x cheaper than models with similar intelligence.

So yeah, the mystery model was Z AI all along. And the bigger story might be that Chinese labs are getting really good at making capable models cheap to run.

----------------------------------------




INSIDE EVERY

IN WHICH DAN PLOTS TO CLONE US ALL

For years, Every CEO Dan Shipper https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVGhlIENhc2UgZm9yIENsb25pbmcgWW91ciBDb3dvcmtlcnMiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUyLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9AZGFuc2hpcHBlciIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo3fQ==’s goal was to automate https://every. editor in chief Kate Lee https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVGhlIENhc2UgZm9yIENsb25pbmcgWW91ciBDb3dvcmtlcnMiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUyLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9Aa2F0ZV8xNzY3IiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjl9’s editorial judgment. The data was there—he had more than 30,000 of her historical edits—but the models weren’t good enough to create a copyediting agent that approached her abilities.

That changed with the launch of GPT-5.6 https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVGhlIENhc2UgZm9yIENsb25pbmcgWW91ciBDb3dvcmtlcnMiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUyLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by92aWJlLWNoZWNrL2dwdC01LTYtc29sIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjEwfQ==. Now, before I file an article, I run it through KateBench, a skill that copyedits based on Kate’s historical edits. Only then does human Kate review the piece, accepting, modifying, or rejecting the agent’s suggestions. Tracked changes in Google Docs catalog those decisions and any additional edits she makes, then Codex rewrites the skill so it compounds. (For more on how KateBench works, read staff writer Katie Parrott https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVGhlIENhc2UgZm9yIENsb25pbmcgWW91ciBDb3dvcmtlcnMiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUyLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9Aa2F0aWUucGFycm90dDEyIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjExfQ==’s writeup https://every. on how engineer Jannik Jung https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVGhlIENhc2UgZm9yIENsb25pbmcgWW91ciBDb3dvcmtlcnMiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUyLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by90ZWFtIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjEzfQ== incorporates feedback to improve its performance.)

https://every. Kate copyediting agent makes suggested changes directly within the Google Doc. (All screenshots courtesy of the author.)




KateBench takes work off Kate’s plate. It also democratizes her expertise—anyone on the team can get a Kate-level quality pass for anything they’ve written. “It’s weirdly hard and specific to copyedit that well,” Dan says. “She’s the only one who can do it at her level, and now that’s not true anymore.”

https://every. self-improves by incorporating data on edits that were accepted versus rejected.




The obvious next step—at least if you’re Dan—is to build a version of KateBench for everyone at the company. That way, COO Brandon Gell https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVGhlIENhc2UgZm9yIENsb25pbmcgWW91ciBDb3dvcmtlcnMiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUyLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9AYnJhbmRvbl81MjYzIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjE2fQ==’s sharp user experience (UX) feedback, head of operations Arielle Shipper https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec

----------
howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy wednesday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* OpenAI’s custom chip is beating Nvidia in early tests

* Anthropic thinks AI is a $30T market

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **VOICES**

## [Is your training data actually model-ready?](https://www.voices.com/solutions/audio-quality-whitepaper?utm_source=ai-valley&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=client_audio-quality-whitepaper_2026)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/432154e1-1076-4b49-a0a9-863f6542d0cb/Newsletter_white_paper__1_.png?t=1787753343)
Follow image link: (https://www.voices.com/solutions/audio-quality-whitepaper?utm_source=ai-valley&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=client_audio-quality-whitepaper_2026)
Caption: Courtesy: Voices

If you're fine-tuning a speech model, you've probably hit this wall: DNSMOS gives you a score, but it doesn't tell you whether the data behind that score is actually right for your model. Treat it as a pass/fail gate and you'll end up training on audio that looks clean on paper but drags down real-world performance while good source data gets tossed for no reason.

Voices' CTO DJ Jalali (with the team's senior audio and voice data engineers) just published a breakdown of the four-step calibration framework they use internally to set model-specific quality thresholds instead of trusting the raw DNSMOS number. It also covers where DNSMOS breaks down and how Voices validates audio for custom datasets at scale.

[Download the White Paper →](https://www.voices.com/solutions/audio-quality-whitepaper?utm_source=ai-valley&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=client_audio-quality-whitepaper_2026)

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e91b59e2-1333-438f-a248-4ae1fa9a4d41/OAIxBroadcom_1920x1080__1___1_.png?t=1787754409)
Caption: 

**1/ OpenAI’s custom chip is beating Nvidia in early tests** - OpenAI published the first benchmarks for [Jalapeño](https://openai.com/index/jalapeno-first-results/), its custom 700W inference chip built with Broadcom. In OpenAI’s [InferenceX tests](https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/openai-jalapeno-better-than-nvidia), it delivered 1.5–1.9x more AI work per watt and 1.7–3.6x lower end-to-end latency than Nvidia’s GB200 and GB300 systems across GPT-OSS 120B, DeepSeek R1 670B and Kimi K2.5 1T.

The interesting thing is OpenAI built it in just nine months, using its own models and Codex during development. It’s not trying to replace Nvidia either. OpenAI still needs Nvidia for training, and Jalapeño is mainly about making inference cheaper and faster.

Two more generations are already in the works, with Jalapeño starting to roll into OpenAI’s data centers later this year and ramping through 2027. So yeah, OpenAI is slowly becoming a chip company too.

Some interesting stuff related to this:

* Why is every AI lab [suddenly](https://www.reddit.com/r/OpenAI/comments/1uhn4y9/why_is_every_ai_lab_suddenly_trying_to_build/) trying to build their own chips?

**2/ Anthropic thinks AI is a $30T market** - Anthropic is [reportedly](https://www.pymnts.com/news/artificial-intelligence/2026/anthropic-readies-30-trillion-dollar-revenue-forecast-investors) telling IPO investors that its total addressable market is more than $30T, based on the amount of work AI models could theoretically do. That’s even bigger than SpaceX’s $28.5T TAM from its IPO filing.

Anthropic’s own numbers are a bit more interesting. Its revenue run rate has already passed $65B, and it’s projecting $190B-$200B in revenue for 2028.

Obviously, TAM numbers are mostly a way to tell investors “this can get really, really big.” But $30T is a pretty insane number. For context, the entire tech sector in the S&P 1500 made about $2.4T last year.

So either AI really is about to eat a huge chunk of the economy, or Anthropic has found the biggest TAM slide ever.


----------

----------
# TRENDING TOOLS

BENCHMARKS DON’T KNOW YOUR JOB https://every.


PLUS: THE NUMBER KATEBENCH TAUGHT US TO COUNT, AND A SIX-AGENT SOLAR CREW HELPING DECIDE WHETHER TO RUN THE DRYER https://every.

by Katie Parrott https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQmVuY2htYXJrcyBEb27igJl0IEtub3cgWW91ciBKb2IiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUxLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9Aa2F0aWUucGFycm90dDEyIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjR9

Midjourney/Every illustration.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQmVuY2htYXJrcyBEb27igJl0IEtub3cgWW91ciBKb2IiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUxLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9hY2NvdW50IiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjV9 to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



AI has a measurement problem. Companies know how much they spend on models and how those models score on public benchmarks. What they often don’t know is whether the models save employees time or produce work people can trust without rechecking. In today’s Context Window is a look at how companies can answer those questions for themselves: We explain why organizations need tests built around real work, show what cloning our editor in chief has taught Every about evals, and meet the six-agent crew helping an Every engineer decide whether his family can run the dryer.



----------------------------------------




SIGNAL

VIBES DON’T SCALE

Suppose your company is spending $100 million a year on AI. You know how much you’re paying—and you know where the models you’re paying for sit on the public leaderboards. But you may still have no idea whether they are doing the jobs you bought them for, or whether a cheaper model would do them just as well. This is a strange way to spend $100 million.

Mercor cofounder and CEO Brendan Foody says https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQmVuY2htYXJrcyBEb27igJl0IEtub3cgWW91ciBKb2IiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUxLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly94LmNvbS9CcmVuZGFuRm9vZHkvc3RhdHVzLzIwOTA1MDA5NDQ5NzkyNDMxODEiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6Nn0= he meets executives at companies in exactly this position: They spend as much as $100 million a year running models without “offline evals,” a fixed set of real tasks used to test and compare models before they touch live work. Box CEO Aaron Levie quote-posted Foody https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQmVuY2htYXJrcyBEb27igJl0IEtub3cgWW91ciBKb2IiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUxLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly94LmNvbS9sZXZpZS9zdGF0dXMvMjA5MTM1OTIyMzM2ODMxNTA1MCIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo3fQ== with the line: “Enterprises will not be able to go just on vibes.”

Public benchmarks can tell you that one model is generally more capable than another. They can’t tell you whether it caught the clause your lawyers care about, preserved your house style, or spared an employee another round of checking. A useful eval starts with the work your company already does: representative cases, failures employees know to look for, and a count of what humans still have to fix.
